Remdesivir use was reported as not significantly different between hEDS patients and matched controls.
MCAS was more than twice as prevalent among hEDS patients with Long COVID compared to those without.
POTS was substantially more prevalent among hEDS patients with Long COVID compared to those without.
ME/CFS was substantially more prevalent among hEDS patients with Long COVID compared to those without.

Co-occurrence of MCAS, POTS, and ME/CFS together was far more common among hEDS patients with Long COVID than in those without, and multi-comorbidity combinations were exceedingly rare in non-hEDS controls.

Cumulative incidence analysis showed that hEDS diagnosis frequently occurred after COVID-19 or Long COVID onset, with markedly elevated cumulative incidence among patients with MCAS, POTS, or ME/CFS comorbidities.

The reverse temporal relationship — cumulative incidence of COVID-19 or Long COVID after an existing hEDS diagnosis — showed only slightly elevated risk with comorbidities, a much weaker effect than the forward (post-viral) direction.
hEDS patients had over seven times the odds of a tuberculosis diagnosis compared to matched controls, driven almost entirely by vertebral tuberculosis coding.
Diagnoses coded as sequelae of infectious disease (ICD B94.8), often used as an early proxy for Long COVID, were more common in patients with hEDS than controls.
Rheumatologic disease diagnoses were substantially more common in hEDS patients than controls, driven mainly by Sjögren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
Autoimmune disorder diagnoses, predominantly autoimmune thyroiditis and immunodeficiency disorders, were substantially more common in hEDS patients than controls.
Chronic lung disease (mainly asthma and COPD) was significantly more common in hEDS patients than matched controls.
Cerebrovascular disease (e.g. transient ischemic attacks, carotid artery obstruction, cerebral aneurysms) was significantly more common in hEDS patients than controls.
Peripheral vascular disease was significantly more common in hEDS patients than in matched controls.
Depression diagnoses were significantly more common among hEDS patients than controls.
Systemic corticosteroid use was significantly more common among hEDS patients than controls, potentially preceding or exacerbating undiagnosed symptoms.
Thalassemia showed a smaller but statistically significant elevation in odds among hEDS patients compared to controls.

Several traditional COVID-19 severity risk factors, including obesity, diabetes, hypertension, liver disease, HIV, substance use disorders, and cancer, were not significantly enriched among hEDS patients compared to controls.
Nearly half of hEDS patients with MCAS who were later diagnosed with hEDS received that hEDS diagnosis after a COVID-19 infection, supporting a role for viral infection as a diagnostic trigger.
At baseline, the most commonly reported PASC symptoms among the 26 study participants were fatigue, brain fog, and shortness of breath.
92% of participants reported being able to perceive or feel qi during the qigong sessions, with sensations including warmth, coolness, tingling, static/electricity, pressure, and magnetism.
73% of participants reported experiencing some improvement in one or more PASC symptoms following the group-based qigong intervention.
72% of participants reported an overall improvement in their energy levels after the qigong intervention.
39% of participants reported improvement in brain fog (concentration/cognitive difficulties) following the qigong intervention.
20% of participants reported improvement in sleep following the qigong intervention.
22 of 26 participants (85%) reported an improvement in their overall well-being as a result of the qigong sessions.

Participants who perceived qi to any extent were more likely to experience PASC symptom improvement (79%) than the two participants who reported no perception of qi, who experienced no symptom improvement at all.
40% of participants reported an increased sense of calmness or relaxation attributable to the qigong sessions, some describing it as a meditative practice.

One participant with frequent arrhythmia episodes reported a marked reduction in episode frequency (from multiple per week to three in one month) during the qigong intervention period, and another participant attributed resolution of atrial fibrillation to normal sinus rhythm to the qigong healing.

One participant reported complete resolution of POTS along with normalized oxygen saturation, return to full-time work, and resolution of pain and fatigue that she attributed to the qigong intervention.

Participants described the group-based format of the qigong sessions—shared experience, community, and validation among people with PASC—as contributing independently to perceived benefit, separate from qigong practice itself.

Flow cytometry of extracellular vesicle surface markers showed that platelet-hyperactivation markers CD29, CD41b, CD42a, and CD69 were significantly overexpressed on EVs from Long COVID patients compared to EVs from healthy controls.
RUNX2 mRNA levels carried in the cargo of Long COVID patient-derived EVs were increased relative to EVs from healthy controls.
Treatment of A549 lung epithelial cells with Long COVID-derived EVs significantly increased RUNX2 mRNA and protein expression compared to cells treated with control EVs.
SESN2 mRNA and protein levels were increased in A549 lung cells treated with Long COVID EVs relative to control EVs, whereas SESN1 levels were unchanged.
Total p53 and phosphorylated p53 (Ser15) protein levels were increased in A549 cells treated with Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs, indicating activation of the p53 stress pathway.
p21 protein and mRNA levels were increased in A549 cells treated with Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs.

Immunofluorescence staining showed significantly increased vimentin and CK19 expression in A549 lung cells treated with Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs, without accompanying increases in migratory capacity, suggesting enhanced fibrotic/EMT-like potential rather than migration.
Scratch assay migration capacity and cell viability of A549 cells did not differ significantly between control-EV and Long Covid-EV treated cells.
Under hyperoxic high-resolution respirometry conditions, A549 cells treated with Long COVID EVs showed significantly higher oxygen consumption than cells treated with control EVs.

Under conditions of increased cell density (metabolic stress), A549 cells treated with Long COVID EVs showed significantly reduced maximal respiration, ATP production, and basal respiration compared to control EV-treated cells, indicating impaired mitochondrial adaptability.
Forced overexpression of RUNX2 in A549 cells was sufficient to activate the p53/p21 pathway and increase SESN2 levels, recapitulating the effects observed with Long Covid EV treatment.

Silencing RUNX2 in A549 cells reduced the stress protein response (p53, p21, SESN2) and restored metabolic stress parameters to control levels even in the presence of Long Covid EVs, demonstrating that RUNX2 mediates the EV-induced stress response.
In silico analysis using TargetScan identified a conserved putative hsa-miR-204-5p binding site within the 3' untranslated region of RUNX2 mRNA.
hsa-miR-204-5p levels were significantly reduced in the cargo of Long Covid EVs compared to control EVs.
Transfection of A549 cells with increasing concentrations of a hsa-miR-204-5p mimic (5-25 nM) dose-dependently decreased RUNX2 protein levels.
Higher concentrations of hsa-miR-204-5p mimic (10-15 nM) also reduced SESN2, p53, and p21 protein levels in A549 cells.

In cells with high pre-existing miR-204 levels, subsequent Long Covid EV treatment induced only a slight increase in RUNX2 and did not significantly alter other stress markers, indicating miR-204 counterbalances the pro-stress effect of LC-EVs.
In IMR90 lung fibroblasts, treatment with Long Covid EVs significantly increased RUNX2 mRNA and protein expression compared to control EVs.
SESN1, SESN2, p53, phospho-p53, and p21 protein levels were all significantly increased in IMR90 fibroblasts treated with Long Covid EVs compared to controls.

In A549 lung cells stressed by increasing cell density, maximal mitochondrial respiration declined significantly in cells treated with Long COVID EVs, while control EV-treated cells maintained stable respiration.
ATP production in A549 cells was reduced at higher cell densities in the presence of Long COVID EVs, indicating impaired energy generation under metabolic stress.
Basal mitochondrial respiration declined in A549 cells at higher cell densities in the presence of Long COVID EVs.
RUNX2 mRNA carried within the cargo of Long COVID-derived EVs was increased compared to control EV cargo.
Forced overexpression of RUNX2 in A549 cells was sufficient to activate the p53/p21 pathway and increase SESN2 levels, recapitulating the phenotype seen with LC-EV treatment.
Silencing RUNX2 in A549 cells attenuated LC-EV-induced increases in RUNX2, SESN2, p53, and p21 protein levels relative to scramble controls.
RUNX2 silencing restored the metabolic stress response of LC-EV-treated cells to levels comparable with scramble/control cells.
In silico TargetScan analysis identified an evolutionarily conserved putative hsa-miR-204-5p binding site in the 3'-UTR of RUNX2 mRNA.
hsa-miR-204-5p levels were lower in the cargo of Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs, consistent with elevated RUNX2 in LC-EVs.
Transfection of A549 cells with a hsa-miR-204-5p mimic (5-25 nM) dose-dependently decreased RUNX2 protein levels.
Higher concentrations of hsa-miR-204-5p mimic (5-15 nM) reduced SESN2, p53, and p21 protein levels in A549 cells.

When A549 cells were transfected with high levels of miR-204 before LC-EV exposure, LC-EVs induced only a slight rise in RUNX2 and stress markers (SESN2, p53, p21) remained largely unchanged, suggesting miR-204 counterbalances the pro-stress effect of RUNX2.
In IMR90 lung fibroblasts, exposure to Long COVID EVs caused a pronounced increase in RUNX2 mRNA and protein expression.
In IMR90 fibroblasts, LC-EV treatment increased SESN1, SESN2, p53, phospho-p53, and p21 protein levels relative to controls.
In IMR90 fibroblasts, LC-EVs reduced maximal respiratory capacity while ATP levels and basal respiration remained unaffected, indicating selective impairment of bioenergetic flexibility.
RUNX2 gene expression and protein levels were higher in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) treated with Long COVID EVs compared to controls.
In endothelial cells, LC-EVs increased SESN2, p53, and p21 levels, while SESN1 levels remained similar between groups.
Aortic smooth muscle cells (ASMC) treated with Long COVID EVs showed upregulation of RUNX2 gene and protein expression compared to controls.
In ASMC, LC-EV treatment increased SESN1, p53, and p21 levels, while SESN2 levels were similar between LC-EV and control groups.
Exposure of IMR90 lung fibroblasts to Long COVID-derived EVs increased RUNX2 mRNA and protein expression compared to control EVs.
SESN1 and SESN2 (sestrin) protein levels were increased in IMR90 fibroblasts treated with Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs.
p53, phosphorylated p53, and p21 protein levels were increased in IMR90 fibroblasts treated with Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs.
Long COVID EVs reduced maximal mitochondrial respiratory capacity in IMR90 fibroblasts, while ATP production and basal respiration remained unchanged.
Long COVID EVs increased RUNX2 mRNA and protein expression in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) compared to control EVs.
In endothelial cells, SESN2, p53 and p21 levels were higher after Long COVID EV treatment compared to controls, while SESN1 levels were similar between groups.
Long COVID EVs increased RUNX2 mRNA and protein expression in aortic smooth muscle cells (ASMC) compared to control EVs.

In ASMC, SESN1, p53 and p21 levels were higher after Long COVID EV treatment while SESN2 levels were similar between groups, contrasting with the SESN2-predominant response seen in lung cells and endothelial cells.

In human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), Long COVID EVs increased RUNX2 and SOX9 gene expression and decreased PPARG2 gene expression compared to control EVs, consistent with a hypoxia-associated osteogenic/mineralization shift.
RUNX2, SESN1, p53 and p21 protein levels were higher in mesenchymal stem cells treated with Long COVID EVs compared to control EVs.

Treatment of A549 cells with protein-rich (non-EV) fractions from either control or Long COVID plasma isolations did not induce significant changes in RUNX2 expression, supporting that the observed effects are attributable specifically to EV cargo rather than co-isolated serum proteins.
The authors caution against using MSC-based cell therapy in Long COVID patients because LC-EVs can alter MSC function toward a profibrotic phenotype, potentially undermining therapeutic efficacy.

Despite similar EV particle quantities between Long COVID and control groups, distinct molecular cargo signatures and functional effects were identified, suggesting that qualitative rather than quantitative changes in EV content contribute to persistence of post-viral symptoms and could serve as a biomarker strategy.
Genomic studies of Long COVID implicate risk loci located within immune and cardiopulmonary pathway genes.
Epigenomic analyses in Long COVID identify differentially methylated regions localized to immune and circadian genes.
Transcriptomic studies show persistent dysregulation of innate immune and coagulation pathways in Long COVID, with reproducible molecular endotypes identified across studies.

Proteomic studies consistently show abnormalities in the complement cascade and coagulation in Long COVID, with a small panel of complement proteins showing highly reproducible changes across independent cohorts.
Metabolomic studies demonstrate sustained mitochondrial dysfunction and altered cellular bioenergetics persisting for up to two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection in Long COVID patients.

Multiomics integration supports the existence of at least two major Long COVID endotypes, one dominated by inflammatory dysregulation and another by metabolic dysregulation, providing a basis for patient stratification.
Machine learning classification models for Long COVID frequently report high performance but are rarely subjected to external validation, limiting confidence in generalizability.

Integration of multiple omics layers supports at least two distinct Long COVID endotypes distinguished by predominant inflammatory versus metabolic dysregulation, providing a basis for patient stratification.
Machine learning classification models built on omics data for Long COVID frequently show high performance but are rarely tested in independent external validation cohorts.
Despite extensive computational omics work, no regulatory-approved diagnostic assay or evidence-based therapeutic intervention for Long COVID has yet emerged from these findings.
More than two-thirds of Long COVID patients reported at least one neurologic symptom 2.5 years after infection, with no significant difference between post-hospitalized and non-hospitalized groups.
Dizziness was significantly more frequent among post-hospitalization Long COVID patients than among non-hospitalized patients.
Fatigue was significantly more prevalent in non-hospitalized Long COVID patients compared with post-hospitalization patients.
Sleep problems were significantly more common in non-hospitalized Long COVID patients than in post-hospitalization patients.
Shortness of breath was significantly more common in post-hospitalization Long COVID patients than in non-hospitalized patients, likely reflecting residual pulmonary/cardiovascular sequelae.
Chest pain was significantly more frequent among non-hospitalized Long COVID patients compared with post-hospitalization patients.
Gastrointestinal symptoms were significantly more frequent among non-hospitalized Long COVID patients compared with post-hospitalization patients.
Objective cognitive impairment measured by MMSE was uncommon overall (about 5%) and did not differ significantly between post-hospitalized and non-hospitalized Long COVID patients.

Abnormal neurologic signs on examination were relatively rare overall but significantly more frequent among non-hospitalized than post-hospitalization Long COVID patients, including short-term memory loss.
Motor dysfunction showed a non-significant trend toward being more prevalent among post-hospitalization compared to non-hospitalized Long COVID patients.

Stress, anxiety, and depression levels assessed via DASS-21 were generally mild and did not differ significantly between post-hospitalization and non-hospitalized Long COVID patients, though rates were higher than general Indian population baselines.
Self-reported anxiety and depression as general symptoms did not differ significantly between post-hospitalization and non-hospitalized Long COVID patients.
Obesity was significantly more prevalent among post-hospitalization Long COVID patients compared to non-hospitalized patients, consistent with known severe COVID-19 risk factors.

Pre-existing lung disease (COPD/asthma) was significantly more prevalent among post-hospitalization patients than non-hospitalized Long COVID patients, suggesting an association between pre-existing respiratory conditions and need for hospitalization.
COVID-19 vaccination rate was significantly higher among non-hospitalized than post-hospitalization patients.

Brain fog, tinnitus, dysgeusia, and blurry vision showed non-significant trends toward being more common among hospitalized (tinnitus, dysgeusia, blurry vision) or non-hospitalized (brain fog) Long COVID patients.
Myalgia, headache, generalized pain, anosmia, and numbness showed no statistically significant differences in prevalence between post-hospitalization and non-hospitalized Long COVID patients.
Mean foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area on OCTA was significantly larger in non-ICU-treated COVID-19 patients than in healthy controls.
FAZ area trended larger in ICU-treated COVID-19 patients versus controls but did not reach statistical significance, likely due to small sample size.
Mean superficial capillary plexus vessel density did not differ significantly between non-ICU, ICU, and control groups.
Mean total macular retinal thickness across ETDRS grid subfields did not differ significantly among non-ICU, ICU, and control groups.
Mean best-corrected visual acuity did not differ significantly among non-ICU, ICU, and control groups, though ICU patients showed a nonsignificant trend toward lower BCVA.
Mean intraocular pressure did not differ significantly among non-ICU, ICU, and control groups.
FAZ area was significantly larger in long-COVID patients with fatigue compared to both patients with no fatigue and healthy controls.

FAZ area measured by OCTA showed poor-to-moderate discriminative ability for detecting fatigue in long-COVID patients, with a calculated positive predictive value of about 40.5% given fatigue prevalence of 23%.
Contrary to expectation, vessel density was significantly greater in patients with extreme fatigue than in patients with no fatigue and controls.
Perifoveal retinal thickness (ETDRS subfields 6-9) was significantly lower in patients without fatigue compared to those with fatigue and to healthy controls.
Mean BCVA, intraocular pressure, and total retinal thickness did not differ significantly among the fatigue subgroups (no fatigue, fatigue, extreme fatigue, control).
Celiac plexus block produced substantial relief of abdominal pain (100%, 80%, and 70% in patients 1-3 respectively) at two-week follow-up in Long COVID patients with refractory GI symptoms.
Durable improvement in GI symptoms (bowel changes/diarrhea) lasted up to 21 months in patients 1 and 2, while patient 3 required repeat CPB every 3 months to maintain benefit.
Following SGB and CPB, all three patients showed reduced dizziness upon standing (orthostatic intolerance) and reduced rapid heartbeat.
Fatigue, depression, and anxiety scores (measured by PROMIS SF-7a, PHQ-9, and GAD-7 respectively) improved in all three patients following treatment.
Some Long COVID patients with persistent GI complaints such as epigastric pain, diarrhea, and constipation did not respond to stellate ganglion block alone.

A UK Biobank cohort study found COVID-19 infection was associated with an elevated hazard ratio for GI dysfunction and pancreatic disease, with pancreatic disease risk increasing further with multiple COVID infections.
A cohort study using the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs database found an increased hazard ratio for developing irritable bowel syndrome 1 year after COVID-19 infection.
A meta-analysis found a pooled prevalence of 15% for IBS following COVID-19 across various countries.
A case-controlled study showed a twofold increased risk of loose stools 5 months after recovery from COVID-19, particularly among those who had diarrhea during acute infection.

Studies show visceral hypersensitivity induces anxiety behavior in a positive feedback loop, and the underlying neuronal pathway requires less stimulus in females, potentially contributing to gender disparity in Long COVID prevalence.

A population-based study found an association between indices of sympathetic activation, autonomic dysfunction, and functional diarrhea, despite sympathetic hyperactivity generally being associated with constipation.
Shortness of breath was the most prevalent long COVID symptom, reported by 10.8% of hospital-discharged COVID-19 survivors.
Persistent fatigue was reported by 9.8% of participants as a long COVID symptom.
Forgetfulness was reported by 9.5% of participants as a long COVID symptom.
Persistent dry cough was reported by 4.3% of participants as a long COVID symptom.
Participants who experienced shortness of breath had significantly lower health-related quality of life scores (EQ-VAS and VR-12 Physical and Mental Component Scores) than those without the symptom.

Participants reporting shortness of breath as a long COVID symptom had significantly lower health-related quality of life scores on the EQ-VAS and VR-12 Physical/Mental Component Scores compared to those without it.

Participants reporting persistent fatigue as a long COVID symptom had significantly lower health-related quality of life scores on the EQ-VAS and VR-12 Physical/Mental Component Scores compared to those without it.

Participants reporting forgetfulness as a long COVID symptom had significantly lower health-related quality of life scores on the EQ-VAS and VR-12 Physical/Mental Component Scores compared to those without it.
Receiving at least three vaccine doses (booster) after COVID-19 infection was associated with lower odds of experiencing shortness of breath as a long COVID symptom.
Receiving at least three vaccine doses (booster) after COVID-19 infection was associated with lower odds of experiencing persistent fatigue as a long COVID symptom.
Receiving at least three vaccine doses (booster) after COVID-19 infection was associated with lower odds of experiencing forgetfulness as a long COVID symptom.
Receiving at least three vaccine doses after COVID-19 infection was associated with lower odds of experiencing forgetfulness as a long COVID symptom.
Receiving at least three vaccine doses after COVID-19 infection was associated with lower odds of experiencing persistent dry cough as a long COVID symptom.
Nearly half of hospitalized COVID-19 patients (49.8%) reported at least one long COVID symptom persisting beyond three months post-infection.

Among those with long COVID at three months, 64.4% (crude) and 65.0% (IPW-weighted) continued to report symptoms one year post-infection, with neurocognitive symptoms such as memory disturbance and peripheral numbness becoming more prominent.
Among participants with persistent long COVID at one year, 22.0% (crude) and 20.9% (IPW-weighted) still reported symptoms at two years post-infection.
Nearly half (46.9%, 69/147) of participants with long COVID symptoms reported that these symptoms significantly impacted their daily living.
After correction for multiple testing, joint pain was the only symptom that remained significantly associated with perceived impact on daily living among long COVID patients.
Severe to critical acute COVID-19 was an independent predictor of developing long COVID, more than doubling the risk compared with non-severe disease.
Complete COVID-19 vaccination (2 or more doses) prior to infection was protective against developing long COVID.
Severe to critical acute COVID-19 was also a significant predictor of long COVID that impacts daily living.
Complete vaccination significantly reduced the risk of long COVID that impacts daily living.
Male sex was associated with a lower risk of long COVID with impact on daily living, implying female sex is a risk factor for more impactful long COVID.

At three months post-infection, participants with long COVID had significantly more problems in mobility, self-care, usual activities, and pain/discomfort domains of the EQ-5D-5L compared to those without long COVID.
At one year post-infection, participants with persistent long COVID had significantly more problems in usual activities and anxiety/depression domains than those without.
At two years post-infection, participants with persistent long COVID had significantly more problems in usual activities and pain/discomfort domains compared to those without persistent symptoms.

Long COVID was associated with significantly lower EQ-5D-5L utility scores at all three follow-up time points, with the magnitude of the difference increasing over time and reaching clinically meaningful thresholds at one and two years.

Utility score trajectories diverged over time: participants with persistent symptoms at one year showed a worsening trend, whereas those whose symptoms resolved by two years showed improved utility scores.
Participants reporting shortness of breath had higher total cognitive complaint and attention impairment scores than those without it, but memory impairment did not differ significantly.
Headache was associated with higher total cognitive complaints and memory impairment but not with attention impairment.
Severe fatigue after mild physical activity was associated with higher total cognitive complaints and higher memory and attention impairment scores.
Abdominal pain, chronic pain, chronic fatigue, and sleep disturbance showed no significant association with total cognitive complaints, memory, or attention impairment.
Difficulty making decisions was significantly more prevalent among male participants than female participants within this Long COVID cohort.
Difficulty retaining new information was significantly more prevalent among female participants than male participants.
Participants reporting confusion were significantly younger than those not reporting confusion.
Difficulty concentrating prevalence varied significantly across education levels, being highest among undergraduates and PhD holders and lowest among bachelor's degree holders.
Participants with under-diploma education reported significantly higher total cognitive complaint and memory impairment severity than those with a bachelor's degree.
Participants with some college/no degree (Undergraduate) education reported significantly higher attention impairment severity than those with bachelor's or master's degrees.
Participants who experienced olfactory/gustatory dysfunction during acute infection had higher memory impairment scores six months later, though attention impairment did not differ.
Severe acute infection showed only a non-significant trend toward higher total cognitive complaints six months later, in a small subgroup.
Duration of olfactory/gustatory dysfunction showed no significant correlation with total cognitive complaints, memory impairment, or attention impairment.
Number of COVID-19 infections showed no significant correlation with total cognitive complaints, memory impairment, or attention impairment.
In a multivariable regression, higher educational attainment independently predicted fewer total cognitive complaints.
In the same multivariable regression, a greater number of physical symptoms independently predicted higher total cognitive complaint scores.
Gender, age, duration of olfactory/gustatory dysfunction, and number of infections were not significant independent predictors of total cognitive complaints in the multivariable regression.

At six months post-infection, self-reported neurocognitive complaints were highly prevalent, with over half of participants reporting difficulty retaining new information and difficulty concentrating, and nearly half reporting memory lapses.
A substantial burden of physical and fatigue-related symptoms was present at six months, with severe post-exertional fatigue and chronic fatigue among the most commonly reported somatic complaints.
No overall gender difference was found in total cognitive complaint scores, contrasting with some prior reports of greater neurological symptom burden among females.
A single 10-minute virtual pet-assisted therapy (VAT) session was associated with a significant reduction in patients' overall long COVID symptom severity score compared with before the session.
Fatigue severity scores were significantly lower immediately after the VAT session compared with before.
Dyspnea severity scores were significantly lower after the VAT session compared with before.
Memory impairment severity scores were significantly lower after the VAT session compared with before.
Tinnitus severity scores were significantly lower after the VAT session compared with before.

Eight other assessed symptoms (generalized pain, muscle pain, limited movement, abdominal symptoms, olfactory dysfunction, gustatory dysfunction, sleep disturbance, and dizziness) showed no significant change after the VAT session.
In multiple regression analysis, patient age, sex, and number of COVID-19 vaccine doses were not significantly associated with the change in total symptom severity score after VAT.

The Canadian Delphi panel prioritized fatigue, post-exertional malaise, cardiovascular issues, respiratory problems, and cognitive impairment (brain fog) as core symptom domains for the Long COVID minimum dataset, consistent with the international Munblit et al Delphi study.

Unlike the Munblit et al international Delphi, this Canadian panel excluded symptoms related to pain, mental health, the nervous system, and the gastrointestinal system from the final minimum dataset.

Care-related topics, including formal/informal care utilisation, quality of care, and barriers/facilitators to care access, achieved consensus early (round 1), a novel contribution not seen in the Munblit et al study where resource-related outcomes failed to reach consensus.
The Delphi process produced a finalized minimum dataset of 48 questions spanning care, quality of life, and symptom domains for use in a Canadian national Long COVID patient registry.
The survey instrument showed strong internal consistency across Delphi rounds, with Cronbach's alpha of 0.903 in round 1 and 0.92 in round 3.
Of 63 participants who provided informed consent, 52 completed all three Delphi rounds, an 82.5% retention rate, though this fell short of the target sample size of 100.

Participants speculated that mental health symptoms were deprioritized partly because attributing psychological symptoms to Long COVID risked invalidating its status as a physical disease, echoing similar stigmatizing conceptualizations historically applied to fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome.
Gastrointestinal symptoms may have received lower priority in the consensus process because they tend to have shorter duration relative to other post-acute Long COVID sequelae.

Based on round 1 open-ended feedback, two new survey elements—'accepting a new way of life' and 'grieving the life one had prior to LC'—were added to the social and emotional well-being section of the quality-of-life domain.

Following round 2 feedback, the quality-of-care category was expanded to explicitly include 'symptoms being recognized (or identified) as LC', reflecting participants' reported difficulty getting Long COVID symptoms recognized and diagnosed by the medical system.

A cited Canadian study found that approximately one in nine adults previously infected with COVID-19 experienced long-term symptoms, and most of these individuals continued to experience symptoms as of June 2023.
Nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation increased whole blood NAD+ levels by an average of 3.1-fold after both 5 and 10 weeks in the NR-NR group.
NAD+ levels remained elevated at 15 (2.6-fold) and 20 weeks (2.1-fold) of continued NR supplementation in the NR-NR group.

Across the included qualitative literature, long COVID was consistently described by patients as an unpredictable, functionally limiting condition marked by fluctuating symptoms, exhausting effort for basic activities, and fear of relapse.

Peer support networks and structured, professionally guided group interventions provided critical emotional and informational validation for people with long COVID, countering isolation and invalidation.
Patients frequently experienced epistemic injustice, with dismissal of their symptoms by healthcare professionals, and women disproportionately reported symptom trivialisation compared with men.

Patients described major difficulty finding reliable information and navigating a disconnected diagnostic and care system, including lack of research, ambiguous advice, and being denied care without positive COVID tests.
Long COVID was experienced as a life-altering event requiring a profound shift in identity, with a non-linear recovery journey and loss of prior social roles and sense of self.

At the second assessment wave, fatigue and pain in other body parts became the predominant long COVID symptoms, affecting 54.8% and 59.2% of residents respectively.
At the third assessment wave, dizziness was the most frequent long COVID symptom, reported by 44.7% of residents.
Partial correlation analysis controlling for age showed that long COVID symptom scores were most strongly correlated between the first and second assessment waves.
In the generalized estimating equations model, being male was associated with lower risk of long COVID symptoms across most organ systems compared with being female.
Individuals who strongly endorsed brain fog had worse baseline cognitive health compared to those who strongly rejected having brain fog.
Participants with brain fog reported more comorbidities than those without brain fog.
Participants with brain fog reported higher levels of COVID-specific and general life stressors than those without brain fog.
Participants with brain fog reported lower levels of social support and salutogenic health habits than those without brain fog.

Individuals with brain fog were more inwardly focused, tended to focus on the negative, compared themselves to external standards, and focused less on improving or adjusting to their situation compared to those without brain fog.

Among participants with brain fog, the unidimensional factor model of the PROMIS-10 Physical Health scale showed lower item means, lower factor loadings, and lower explained variance compared to those without brain fog.
There was evidence of measurement non-invariance and differential item functioning (DIF) for the fatigue item of the PROMIS-10 scale between those with and without brain fog.

Self-reported regained work ability (mWAI1) declined slightly from 89.1% at 6-12 months to 88.0% at 24 months post-infection, indicating persistent impairment of work capacity two years after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Task-related work ability (mWAI2) dropped substantially from 90.4% pre-infection to 79.1% at 6-12 months and remained reduced at 79.9% at 24 months post-infection.
The proportion of participants with poor regained work ability (mWAI1 ≤60%) increased slightly from 7.4% at baseline to 8.5% at 24-month follow-up.
Participants with poor work ability (mWAI1 ≤60%) at 24 months had substantially longer sick leave than those with moderate or excellent work ability.

Stratified analysis showed statistically significantly lower mWAI1 at follow-up among older participants and among those without comorbid mental disorders, with distinct patterns between mental and physical task groups.
The incidence rate of health-related change in working hours was higher among part-time employees than full-time employees.

Only 62.7% of participants reported excellent regained work ability at both 6-12 and 24 months, while about 10.0% showed a decline from unimpaired to impaired work ability, and 14.4% reported moderate or poor work ability at both time points.
Among post-COVID symptom clusters, participants with smell/taste disorders had the shortest sick leave duration while those with chest symptoms had the longest.

In mutually adjusted regression, older age, low school education, current smoking, obesity, physical working tasks, and medical treatment during the acute index infection were all independently associated with lower task-related work ability (mWAI2) at 24 months.
All post-COVID symptom clusters present at 24 months were associated with lower mWAI2, with fatigue and neurocognitive impairment showing the strongest negative associations.
Female sex was associated with lower task-related work ability (mWAI2) among participants younger than 40 years but showed no association in those 40 years or older.
Current smoking was associated with lower task-related work ability (mWAI2) in younger participants but not in older participants.
Physical working tasks were a significant risk factor for lower mWAI2 among older participants but not among younger participants.
The fatigue symptom cluster was strongly associated with lower mWAI2 in both younger and older age groups.
Neurocognitive impairment was strongly associated with lower mWAI2 in both younger and older age groups, representing one of the strongest overall risk factors.
The anxiety/depression/sleep disorder symptom cluster was significantly associated with lower mWAI2 in both younger and older age groups.
Pre-existing comorbid mental disorders were linked to reduced mWAI2 in both younger and older participants, with a somewhat stronger effect in older participants.
Older age was a risk factor for lower mWAI2 in both mentally and physically working participants, but the effect was more pronounced among those with physical working tasks.
Further SARS-CoV-2 infections after the index infection were significantly associated with lower mWAI2 only among physically working participants, not among mentally working participants.
Female sex was positively associated with mWAI2 among participants with comorbid mental disorders but negatively associated among those without such comorbidities.

Older age was associated with lower task-related work ability among both mentally and physically working participants, but the negative effect of age was more pronounced among those with physical working tasks.
Further SARS-CoV-2 reinfections during follow-up were statistically significantly associated with lower task-related work ability only among participants with physically demanding jobs.

Female sex was positively associated with task-related work ability among participants with comorbid mental disorders but negatively associated among those without such comorbidity, indicating effect modification by mental comorbidity.
Female sex was statistically significantly associated with fewer weeks of sick leave at 24 months.
Further SARS-CoV-2 infections during follow-up were statistically significantly associated with fewer weeks of sick leave.
Comorbid cardiovascular disease was associated with a longer duration of sick leave at 24 months.
Comorbid mental disorders were associated with a longer duration of sick leave at 24 months, the largest effect among comorbidities examined.
The fatigue symptom cluster reported at 24 months showed the strongest positive association with sick leave duration among the symptom clusters examined.
The musculoskeletal pain symptom cluster reported at 24 months was positively associated with sick leave duration.
The neurocognitive impairment symptom cluster reported at 24 months was positively associated with sick leave duration, though with a smaller effect than fatigue or musculoskeletal pain.
Age, education, smoking, obesity, and type of working task were not statistically significantly associated with sick leave duration in the adjusted model.
Post-exertional malaise was strongly associated with reduced task-related work ability in mutually adjusted models.
Suspected ME/CFS, screened using the DSQ-PEM instrument, was strongly associated with reduced task-related work ability in mutually adjusted models.

Participants with comorbid mental disorders had a substantially lower rate of consistently excellent work ability across both follow-up time points and higher rates of persistently moderate or poor work ability compared to those without such comorbidities.
The negative association between current smoking and task-related work ability was stronger among younger participants than among older participants.
The incidence rate of health-related change in working hours was higher among part-time employees than full-time employees.
Among symptom clusters, the chest symptoms cluster was associated with the longest mean sick leave duration, while the smell/taste cluster was associated with the shortest.
Fatigue, dyspnea, and reduced exercise tolerance prevalence declined substantially from 3 to 12 months post-discharge, representing roughly a two-thirds reduction in prevalence.
Cardiac symptoms showed an early significant decline between 3 and 6 months, unlike other minor persistent symptoms.
Persistence of dyspnea at 12 months was significantly higher in patients with critical initial illness compared to moderate illness.
Reduced exercise tolerance at 12 months followed a similar severity-dependent pattern, being much more common in critically ill survivors.
Activated T cells (CD3+HLA-DR+) declined progressively from 3 to 12 months, indicating resolution of T-cell hyperactivation.
CD3+CD8+ cytotoxic T cell counts decreased significantly between 3 and 12 months post-discharge.
The CD4/CD8 ratio showed a gradual upward trend over follow-up, consistent with immune homeostasis restoration.
NK cells and B cells were stable at the group level across follow-up, but a subset of about 20% of patients showed persistently low NK counts at all visits.
Complement C3c levels rose progressively over the 12-month follow-up, paradoxically increasing as clinical symptoms improved.
Complement C4 showed only minor transient fluctuations across the 12-month follow-up, unlike C3c.
Serum IgA levels rose significantly and remained elevated throughout the 12-month follow-up, suggesting sustained mucosal immune activation.
IgM declined modestly over follow-up while IgG and IgE remained stable.
At 3 months, patients with fatigue had significantly lower NK cell counts than those without fatigue.
At 3 months, patients with fatigue had significantly higher CD3+ T-cell percentages than those without fatigue.
At 6 months, patients with dyspnea had significantly lower NK cell counts than those without dyspnea.
At 6 months, patients with dyspnea had significantly higher CD3+CD4+ T-cell percentages than those without dyspnea.
At 12 months, patients with myalgia/arthralgia had lower total lymphocyte, CD3+, CD3+CD4+, and CD19+ cell counts than those without.
At 3 months, patients with cardiac symptoms had significantly higher complement C3c levels than those without cardiac symptoms.

At 12 months, patients with fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance had lower C3c than asymptomatic peers, contrasting with the earlier association of higher C3c with cardiac symptoms, suggesting complex, phase-specific complement dynamics.

The 'Respiratory' immune-symptom endotype, characterized by dyspnea and reduced exercise tolerance, showed lower NK-cell counts/percentages and higher CD3/CD4 at 6 months, higher C3c early with cardiopulmonary complaints, but lower C3c by 12 months among those with fatigue/reduced exercise tolerance, and higher IgM at 6 months among those with dyspnea.
The 'Neurocognitive' immune-symptom endotype, defined by cognitive dysfunction/memory impairment, displayed elevated activated T cells at month 3 compared with those without cognitive symptoms.

The 'Musculoskeletal' immune-symptom endotype, comprised of participants with myalgia/arthralgia at 12 months, was distinguished by lower total lymphocytes with reduced CD3+, CD3+CD4+, and CD19+ counts, suggesting broader low-grade immune insufficiency.
Patients who had been critically ill showed a slower decline in activated T cells and more prolonged suppression of CD3+CD4+ and CD3+CD8+ T cells compared to those with moderate or severe illness.
Patients recovering from critical COVID-19 maintained significantly higher IgM levels than those with severe disease across all three follow-up timepoints.
IgG levels were higher in the critical illness group compared to the severe group at month 3.
Patients who had been critically ill maintained significantly higher serum IgM levels than those with severe disease across all three follow-up timepoints (3, 6, and 12 months).
IgG levels were higher in patients recovering from critical COVID-19 compared to those with severe disease at the 3-month timepoint.
Complement C3c levels increased across all initial severity groups over follow-up, but the rise was more pronounced in patients who had severe or critical COVID-19.
Patients who had been critically ill showed a slower decline in activated T cells and more prolonged suppression of both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells compared to patients with moderate or severe illness.
Total lymphocyte counts remained within the normal reference range throughout the 12-month follow-up period.

The three immune-symptom endotypes and their distinguishing immune features remained stable after sensitivity analyses using only 6-month data and after residualizing immune markers for age, sex, BMI, and initial disease severity.
The respiratory (complement/NK-suppressed) immune endotype was over-represented among survivors of critical illness, who also showed slower decline of activated T cells.

Feedback from the first five patients enrolled in the intervention arm indicated poor tolerance of adapted physical activity sessions, even at the lowest exertion thresholds, and poor adherence to the cognitive-behavioral rationale for symptom persistence, prompting early modifications to the rehabilitation protocol.
Nearly half of children evaluated at least 6 months after COVID-19 recovery had abnormal spirometry, predominantly a restrictive lung pattern.
Children reporting persistent post-COVID symptoms had nearly twice the risk of abnormal spirometry results compared with those without persistent symptoms.
Children who had moderate-to-critical initial COVID-19 severity had a significantly higher risk of abnormal spirometry results than those with asymptomatic/mild disease.
Undernourished children (BMI-for-age z-score < -2 SD) had a significantly higher risk of abnormal spirometry results than normally nourished children.
In multivariate logistic regression, moderate-to-critical COVID-19 severity independently predicted more than fivefold higher odds of impaired pulmonary function.
In multivariate logistic regression, undernourishment independently predicted more than fivefold higher odds of impaired pulmonary function after COVID-19.

The number of persistent symptoms reported (single vs. multiple) was not statistically significantly associated with abnormal spirometry results, despite 11 of 12 subjects with multiple symptoms showing abnormal spirometry.
History of hospitalization for the initial COVID-19 episode was not significantly associated with decreased respiratory function in this cohort.
Among spirometry parameters, FEV1 showed a median predicted value of 77.9%, below the 80% normal threshold, indicating mild reduction in expiratory flow in a subset of children after COVID-19.
Fatigue was the most common persistent symptom reported by children after recovering from COVID-19, present among the 18% of subjects with persistent symptoms.
Ventilator support during initial COVID-19 was not significantly associated with impaired lung function, although 3 of 4 (75%) ventilated subjects showed abnormal spirometry.
Propranolol may improve social anxiety in individuals with autism spectrum disorder based on reviewed studies.
Propranolol may improve verbal problem-solving ability in ASD according to reviewed studies.
Propranolol may improve cognitive flexibility in individuals with ASD.
Propranolol may improve emotional regulation in ASD according to reviewed studies.
Propranolol may reduce behavioral dysregulation in individuals with ASD.
Propranolol has been described to produce benefits in facial scanning behavior in ASD.
Propranolol has been described to produce benefits in verbal fluency in ASD.
Propranolol may attenuate adrenergic hyperarousal and promote parasympathetic dominance in individuals with autism spectrum disorder.
Pharmacogenetic factors, including unspecified polymorphisms, are proposed as potential tools to inform patient selection for propranolol treatment in ASD.
Autonomic biomarkers are suggested as a potential means of identifying ASD patients likely to benefit from propranolol treatment.
The most consistent evidence for propranolol in ASD supports anxiolytic effects specifically under sustained dosing, while cognitive and behavioral benefits remain preliminary.
Propranolol's central nervous system penetration and anxiolytic profile support its potential use as an adjunctive therapy in selected ASD cases when other strategies are insufficient.
Following NESA neuromodulation, children with ASD showed a 7% (4-point) reduction in overall Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) scores, indicating improved sleep.
The sleep-disordered breathing subscale of the CSHQ (snoring/apnea related items) remained unchanged after NESA treatment, unlike other sleep subscales.
The Aberrant Behavior Checklist (ABC-C) total scores decreased by 12 points (25%) after NESA treatment, indicating fewer problematic behaviors in every subscale examined.
Sensory Profile (SP-2) scores were 12% lower after NESA treatment, indicating reduced sensory reactivity and improved sensory processing patterns.
Parents' Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores decreased by 1.83 points (21%) after their child's NESA treatment, though the change was not statistically significant.

Among the four NESA protocols tested, Protocol E (15 sessions, 45 min, directional electrode changed mid-treatment, focused on Program 7) produced superior results across all tests with minimal within-group variability.

Protocol C (20 sessions, 45 min each, applied to a single subject older than 16) produced the most favorable outcomes of all protocols, particularly on the ABC-C where scores differed by 9 or more points from other protocols.

Protocol A (20 sessions, 30 min, for participants living near the clinic) also showed satisfactory ABC-C scores, with patients 11 and 07 (both on Protocol A) showing mean improvements of 19% and 27% respectively across all instruments.
A minority of participants (patients 09, 10, 03, and particularly patient 05) showed worsening scores after NESA treatment, with an overall negative change of about -4.5%.
Among the 12 children with ASD completing the study, 75% had additional medical problems, most commonly sleep disturbances and gastrointestinal complaints.
75% of the study participants were under pharmacological treatment, including stimulants, risperidone, melatonin, and other psychotropic or metabolic agents.
No adverse effects or discomfort were reported during NESA sessions across all protocols, supporting the feasibility and tolerability of the intervention in this pediatric ASD population.
Of 14 participants who initiated the NESA study, 12 (86%) completed all scheduled sessions, with dropout minimal and unrelated to the intervention.
21.5% of adult COVID-19 patients reported symptoms consistent with PASC (symptoms lasting less than 3 months post-infection).
8.8% of adult COVID-19 patients reported Long COVID (symptoms persisting ≥3 months post-infection).
10.5% of pediatric COVID-19 patients reported symptoms consistent with PASC.
9% of pediatric COVID-19 patients reported Long COVID.
Age of 54 years or older was a predictor of PASC in adults.
Female sex was a significant predictor of PASC in adult patients.
Non-Caucasian race was identified as a predictor of PASC in adult patients.
Smoking was associated with increased likelihood of PASC in adult patients.
Obesity was a predictor of PASC in adult patients.
Pneumonia as an acute complication was a predictor of PASC in adult patients.
Having multiple comorbidities was a predictor of PASC in adult patients.
A higher red blood cell count was protective against development of PASC in adult patients.
Female sex was associated with Long COVID (symptoms ≥3 months) in adult patients.
Obesity was associated with Long COVID in adult patients.
Pre-existing heart disease was identified as a predictor of Long COVID in adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Female sex was a significant predictor of PASC among pediatric patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Presence of comorbidities was a predictor of PASC in pediatric patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Younger age (10 years or younger) was a significant predictor of Long COVID in pediatric patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Identity transformation, involving a reconceptualisation of beliefs, values and roles, was identified as the central mechanism underlying the Long COVID Rehabilitation Intervention's effect on self-perception, occupational choices, and engagement in meaningful activities.

Acceptance of one's illness and situation was found to be an overarching mechanism operating across all four programme theory components (identity transformation, person-centred care, patient education, and peer support).

A person-centred, multidisciplinary (physiotherapy and occupational therapy) approach with a trustful patient-professional relationship was associated with patients feeling acknowledged and led to a more coherent rehabilitation course with strengthened commitment and engagement.

Patient education on energy management and breathing techniques, delivered with opportunities for reflection with health professionals and peers, was associated with improved symptom management, better planning of daily activities and increased participation in everyday life.

Participation in the energy management peer group, where patients interacted with others with similar long COVID symptoms, enhanced understanding and acceptance of symptoms and reduced feelings of isolation, whereas the relaxation/respiration and cardio workout groups (individually focused) did not foster this peer effect.

Peer support benefits were diminished for patients whose predominant symptoms were physical/muscular or cognitive rather than fatigue, or who had severe fatigue, as they found it harder to relate to other group members, potentially increasing rather than reducing feelings of isolation.

Lack of understanding and support from relatives acted as a sociocultural contextual barrier that constrained patients' ability to activate the acceptance mechanism and implement rehabilitation strategies.

Flexible work conditions and supportive managers/colleagues facilitated patients' ability to implement energy-management strategies at work, whereas rigid work roles and unsupportive workplace norms created a dilemma limiting strategy implementation.
Long COVID is characterised by persistent, debilitating symptoms including fatigue, cognitive impairment, muscle pain, and dyspnoea that can linger for months after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Females were overrepresented among both the study's patient participants (10 of 12) and in the broader documented incidence/prevalence of long COVID, contributing to recruitment challenges in obtaining male informants.

Health professionals reported shifting their clinical focus from curing patients to helping them manage and cope with long COVID symptoms, contrasting with the general societal norm of pushing through illness to recover.
A meta-analysis of studies through 2022 found that Long COVID-related symptoms affect approximately 43% of COVID-19 subjects worldwide.
A cross-sectional study using a limited LC definition reported a higher prevalence of COVID-19 sequelae in individuals who had both periodontitis and obesity compared to those with obesity alone.
Dendritic cells are the main source of type I interferon in gingival tissue, with higher levels found in subjects with periodontitis.
Studies on Herpesviruses and periodontitis showed lower interferon levels in periodontitis patients testing positive for these viruses or during active periodontitis.

Acute COVID-19 is characterized by functional impairment of adaptive immunity, with decreased total B cells, CD4+ T cells, and CD8+ T cells (lymphopenia), accompanied by functionally exhausted T cells.
Th17 effector cytokines, primarily IL-17A and IL-22, play crucial roles in the pathogenesis of both COVID-19 and periodontitis.
CD8+ T cells appear to help preserve alveolar bone by suppressing osteoclastogenesis in chronic periodontitis, but their protective role may be masked by the overreactive immune response of LC.

MPO-DNA levels, a marker of neutrophil extracellular traps, positively correlate with probing depths and clinical attachment loss, with the highest levels seen in individuals with both periodontitis and rheumatoid arthritis.

Hyperactivation of monocytes and macrophages has been reported in Long COVID, with active monocytes detected persisting from eight to fifteen months regardless of the severity of the initial infection.
In vitro assays with macrophages from subjects recovered from COVID-19 have demonstrated persistent hyperregulation of inflammatory molecule production and downregulation of pro-resolving factors.
Elevated systemic IL-6 levels in COVID-19 prompted the use of IL-6 inhibitors, such as tocilizumab and siltuximab, as therapeutic drugs against COVID-19.
Elevated IL-6 levels in gingival crevicular fluid are linked to alveolar bone loss and dysbiotic biofilms in periodontitis.
Higher titers of plasma ACE2 activity have been observed in individuals with Long COVID for up to four months following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.
In cross-sectional epidemiologic studies, no association was found between long-term salivary SARS-CoV-2 shedding and Long COVID or persistent gastrointestinal disease.

SARS-CoV-2 presence in the olfactory mucosa was linked to local Long COVID symptoms, while SARS-CoV-2 was also detected in supra- and subgingival biofilms of individuals with acute COVID-19, even in the absence of periodontitis.

Epstein-Barr virus reactivation/co-infection during COVID-19 is considered a potential factor in Long COVID, associated with neurocognitive symptoms such as fatigue, and EBV is separately linked to periodontitis with a positive correlation between EBV presence, gingival inflammation, and probing depths.
Autoantibodies against type I interferon were reported not to be associated with Long COVID, contrasting with claims that COVID-driven autoimmunity against IFN-1 contributes to LC pathophysiology.

Individuals with Long COVID show an imbalance in terminal complement complex formation, with elevated soluble C5bC6 complexes, diminished C7-containing TCC, and associated thrombo-inflammation including tissue injury, red blood cell lysis, platelet activation, and monocyte-platelet aggregates.
A single nucleotide polymorphism in the genes coding for complement C5 and C3 has been linked to periodontitis.

MMP-1, MMP-8, and MMP-9 are significantly elevated in Long COVID and correlate with disease severity, neutrophil degranulation, endothelial dysfunction, metabolic dysregulation, and pulmonary fibrosis; MMP-8 is also a major collagen-degrading enzyme in periodontitis.
Bemquerer et al. (2024) found no significant changes in the composition of subgingival pathogens when evaluating periodontitis in individuals with acute COVID-19.
Haran et al. (2021) observed that higher early levels of Prevotella and Veillonella in acute COVID-19 patients were associated with prolonged symptoms and the eventual development of Long COVID.

A case-control study found increased salivary IL-6 measured at two time points in individuals with both COVID-19 and periodontitis, while periodontitis alone was associated with elevated salivary RANKL and IL-1β.

Individuals with acute COVID-19 had a subsequent increase in the serum RANKL/OPG ratio compared with healthy controls, and in a mouse model, murine coronavirus (MHV-3) caused an osteoporotic phenotype through TNF by infecting macrophages and osteoclasts.
A recent study demonstrated that COVID-19 can induce oropharyngeal dysbiosis that persists for at least 30 days, independent of viral clearance or antibiotic exposure.

A scoping review suggests that periodontitis and COVID-19 may independently raise serum levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in the same individual, though combined or causal effects between the two diseases remain unclear.
Among nine symptoms robustly associated with PASC, anosmia/ageusia and fatigue were identified as the most influential in the data-driven definition.
A static PASC scoring system with an optimal threshold of 13 classified 19% of SARS-CoV-2-infected participants versus 4% of controls as PASC positive.
Using a dynamic scoring framework tracking six-month intervals, 33% of infected participants were classified as PASC positive at the same threshold, reflecting temporal fluctuation in symptom burden.
Symptom burden among infected participants peaked at 0-5 months post-infection and declined thereafter over the follow-up period.

Participants with long covid reported more real-world aches and fatigue symptoms during ecological momentary assessment than those without long covid, and this association remained after controlling for baseline mental health.
Long covid status was not associated with real-world respiratory symptoms measured via ecological momentary assessment.
Greater within-subject aches/fatigue symptoms were concurrently associated with higher momentary negative affect.
Greater within-subject aches/fatigue symptoms were concurrently associated with higher interpersonal problems.
Greater within-subject aches/fatigue symptoms were concurrently associated with lower momentary positive affect.
Aches/fatigue symptoms prospectively predicted greater subsequent negative affect.
Aches/fatigue symptoms prospectively predicted lower subsequent positive affect.
Across all participants, higher subjective cognitive fatigue scores were associated with flatter (lower) frontal EEG aperiodic exponent values, indicating a shift toward cortical excitation.
A one-way ANOVA showed a significant overall main effect of group (HC, LCOF, MS+F, MS-F) on frontal aperiodic exponent values.
Individuals with MS and fatigue (MS+F) showed significantly lower (flatter) frontal aperiodic exponent values than healthy controls.
Individuals with Long-COVID-related fatigue (LCOF) showed significantly lower (flatter) frontal aperiodic exponent values than healthy controls.
A planned transdiagnostic contrast showed that pooled fatigued participants (MS+F and LCOF) had significantly lower frontal aperiodic exponent values than healthy controls.
The same planned contrast showed pooled fatigued participants had significantly lower frontal aperiodic exponent values than a pooled non-fatigued group (HC and MS-F).
In a supplementary occipital region of interest, no significant group differences in aperiodic exponent were found, supporting the frontal specificity of the fatigue-related effect.
In a logistic mixed-effects model, lower frontal aperiodic exponent values significantly predicted higher likelihood of belonging to the fatigued group.
Higher depression scores (BDI-FS) significantly predicted greater likelihood of belonging to the fatigued group in the logistic regression model.
Age was not a significant predictor of fatigue status in the logistic regression model.
Adding the frontal aperiodic exponent to a model with age and depression significantly improved model fit for classifying fatigue status, with lower AIC and higher pseudo-R2.
The full logistic regression model (aperiodic exponent, age, depression) achieved good classification performance for fatigue status with an AUC of 0.78, sensitivity of 71%, and specificity of 74%.
A model using only the frontal aperiodic exponent as predictor showed moderate standalone discriminatory power for fatigue status, with AUC of 0.68.
Plasma TNF, CCL2 and CXCL11 were persistently elevated in individuals with long COVID compared with non-infected controls for up to 9 months post-infection.
Plasma TNF protein levels showed a statistically significant negative correlation with arterial oxygenation (pO2) in individuals with long COVID, significant in LCAM but not LCAS up to month 8.9.
TNF mRNA was persistently upregulated across most immune cell types and time points in individuals with LCAM.
LCAM samples showed persistent upregulation of the TNF signaling pathway across CD4+, CD8+ T cells, B cells and CD14+/CD16+ monocytes compared with acute infection, up to month 8.9.
LCAM samples showed persistent downregulation of interferon (IFN) signaling and response pathways across major immune cell subsets compared with acute infection, up to month 8.9.
TGFβ and WNT–β-catenin signaling activity in CD14+ monocytes showed a modest positive correlation with fatigue (FAS) scores in individuals with long COVID.
IFNα/IFNβ induction pathway activity in CD8+ T cells and NK cells positively correlated with FAS (fatigue) scores in long COVID.

LCAM samples showed significantly increased abundance of CD69hiCD27hi GZMK+ CD8+ T cell (cluster C3) and CD69+TGFB1+ GZMK+ NK cell (cluster C2) neighborhoods compared with acute infection and recovered individuals.

A distinct CD14+ monocyte subcluster (MC4), marked by high IRF1, IRF8, TGFB1, CTNNB1, ENG and NOTCH1 expression, was consistently and significantly increased in LCAM compared with acute infection and recovered individuals, defining the 'LC-Mo' state.
MC4 proportion within CD14+ monocytes showed a modest but statistically significant positive correlation with FAS (fatigue) score and a negative correlation with pO2.
Individuals with long COVID and high MC4 proportion (MC4hi, >10% of CD14+ monocytes) exhibited significantly greater fatigue than those with low MC4 proportion (MC4lo) or recovered individuals (RLC).

In an independent validation cohort, individuals with respiratory PASC and bronchial hyper-responsiveness (Resp-PASC-BHR) showed significantly higher LC-Mo signature expression in monocyte cluster Clust1 than those with respiratory PASC alone, supporting a link between LC-Mo and progression to severe respiratory disease.

Flow cytometry showed a significant increase in CD14+ monocyte percentage among PBMCs in individuals with long COVID compared with recovered acute COVID-19 and non-infected donors, independent of acute severity.

Median fluorescence intensity of HLA-DQ, CD120b, CALR, CD99 and TGFB1 was significantly higher on CD14+ monocytes from individuals with long COVID compared with recovered/non-infected donors, while HLA-DR, CD51, CD105, IRF8, IFNGR1 and CD163 showed no significant difference.
TGFβ1 protein expression (MFI) on CD14+ monocytes inversely correlated with blood pO2 in individuals with long COVID.

Chromatin accessibility analysis showed persistent AP-1 family motif activity in CD8+ T cells and NK cells, and elevated AP-1 motif accessibility in CD14+ monocytes up to month 5.9 in LCAM, after which enrichment shifted toward SP1/KLF transcription factors.

Individuals with severe acute infection (LCAS) retained an acute-COVID-19-like transcriptomic profile in PBMCs, in contrast to LCAM in which acute-infection gene signatures declined by months 6-8.9, reflecting immune heterogeneity based on acute infection severity.
CD14+ monocytes from LCAS individuals showed upregulated PD-1 signaling and MHC class II antigen presentation pathways compared to acute infection samples, but not compared to recovered individuals.
NK cells from LCAM individuals showed distinctly increased expression of SREBF1, TAGLN2, TNIP1, NFKBIA and CD83 compared to NK cells from recovered and acute-infection individuals.
TGFβ and WNT-β-catenin signaling activity in CD14+ monocytes showed a modest positive correlation with fatigue (FAS) scores in LC patients, strengthening when recovered LC individuals were included.
IFNα/IFNβ induction pathway activity in CD8+ T cells and NK cells positively correlated with fatigue (FAS) scores in both LC-only and combined LC-plus-recovered analyses.

WNT-β-catenin signaling in CD8+ T cells and TLR signaling cascades in NK cells also correlated with fatigue (FAS) scores, while TNF signaling in these same cells did not show a significant correlation.
A higher proportion of MC1 CD14+ monocytes (the IL1B+/NFKB1+/MHC-II-high inflammatory subcluster) was negatively correlated with fatigue (FAS) scores.
Long COVID individuals with high proportions of the LC-Mo (MC4) monocyte state (MC4hi) exhibited significantly greater fatigue than those with low MC4 proportions (MC4lo) or recovered individuals.
Flow cytometry showed consistently higher median fluorescence intensity of CALR, CD120b, HLA-DQ and TGFβ1 on CD14+ monocytes in long COVID individuals with more severe fatigue and dyspnea symptoms.
TGFβ1 protein expression (MFI) on CD14+ monocytes inversely correlated with arterial oxygenation (pO2) in long COVID patients.
Protein levels of TGFβ1 and IRF8 on CD14+ monocytes positively correlated with each other in long COVID patients, consistent with coexpression within the LC-Mo state.

In bronchoalveolar lavage/PBMC integrated myeloid clusters, the CI4 cluster (highest LC-Mo and profibrotic signature) upregulated SPP1, CCL13, CCL2 and FOLR2 relative to CI5 or CI6 clusters, in both respiratory-PASC and non-respiratory-PASC individuals.

After ex vivo bacterial (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) stimulation, CD14+ monocytes from LCAM individuals showed significant downregulation of inflammatory response, IFNγ signaling, IL-10 signaling, cytokine signaling and IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling pathways compared to stimulated monocytes from recovered individuals.
Among stimulated CD14+ monocytes, DHFR, HMOX1, EREG and GCLC were among the top genes significantly upregulated in LC-Mohi versus LC-Molo donors after Pseudomonas aeruginosa stimulation.
Interferon response genes IRF9, ASCC3, XAF1, SAMD9L, LILRB4 and CGAS were downregulated in stimulated LC-Mohi monocytes compared to LC-Molo, indicating a blunted interferon response.

Chromatin accessibility motif analysis showed FOXO, TCF (especially TCF7L2) and ZIC transcription factor motifs were more accessible in stimulated LC-Mohi monocytes, whereas ETS and AP-1 motifs were more accessible in stimulated LC-Molo monocytes.

The open chromatin landscape of the MC4/LC-Mo monocyte subcluster showed the highest enrichment for ETS family transcription factor motifs (GABPA, ETV1, ETV4, SPI1, SPIC), correlating with expression of proangiogenic/adhesion genes (VEGFA, ENG, TGFB1, RXRA, ICAM1, ITGA5) and disease-associated genes (TTC7A, LMNA, IER3).

Later studies confirmed the lack of association with major congenital malformations, or found that any significantly elevated unadjusted risk was no longer significant after adjustment for covariates and confounds.

Anytime gestational exposure to pregabalin was generally not associated with significantly elevated risk of stillbirth, low birth weight, preterm birth, small for gestational age, low Apgar score, or microcephaly, though some unadjusted or non-disease-control comparisons showed elevated risk that did not persist after adjustment or against disease controls.

Anytime gestational exposure to pregabalin showed either no increased risk of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and related disorders, or a significantly increased unadjusted risk that became non-significant after adjustment for covariates and confounds.

Pregabalin does not act on GABA receptors but instead inhibits calcium influx into neurons via the α2δ-1 subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing release of excitatory neurotransmitters and underlying its sedative, anxiolytic, and anticonvulsant properties.
An estimated 0.04% to 0.14% of women use pregabalin at some point during pregnancy.

During anterior lumbar interbody fusion, the patient developed severe bradycardia progressing to cardiac arrest, most likely due to hyper vagal stimulation from surgical manipulation near the superior hypogastric plexus and forceful peritoneal retraction in this morbidly obese patient.

Administration of 6 mg IV ephedrine increased the patient's heart rate from 50-55 bpm to 75-85 bpm and blood pressure from 78/40 to 100/60 mmHg during the initial bradycardic episode, though bradycardia later recurred and progressed to cardiac arrest.
RMSSD, a time-domain vagally-mediated HRV measure, did not significantly differ between boys with ASD and typically developing boys.
pNN50, a vagally-mediated HRV measure, did not significantly differ between boys with ASD and typically developing boys.
High-frequency (HF) power, a vagally-mediated HRV measure, did not significantly differ between boys with ASD and typically developing boys.
Alpha2-band EEG coherence between posterior temporal channels T5 and T6 was lower in boys with ASD than TD boys before multiple-comparison correction, but this did not survive FDR correction.
Beta1-band EEG coherence was higher in boys with ASD than TD boys at several channel pairs (F3–O1, F3–F4, F7–F8, O1–O2), a pattern of local hypercoherence that did not survive FDR correction.
Beta2-band EEG coherence was higher in boys with ASD than TD boys at F7–F8 and O1–O2, but this did not survive FDR correction.

Beta1-band EEG coherence between posterior temporal channels T5 and T6 was significantly reduced in boys with ASD compared to TD boys, and this remained significant after FDR correction, making it the study's primary finding.
Within the ASD group, beta1 coherence (T5-T6) was positively correlated with RMSSD, an index of vagally-mediated heart rate variability.
Within the ASD group, lower beta1 coherence (T5-T6) was associated with lower SRS social motivation subscale scores (indicating greater social motivation impairment).

pNN50 significantly moderated the negative relationship between beta1 coherence (T5-T6) and SRS social motivation scores, attenuating this negative association at higher pNN50 levels, though pNN50 itself did not independently predict social motivation.
Chronic intranasal oxytocin did not change the overall duration of fixations directed toward the face of a live interaction partner compared to placebo.

Four weeks of oxytocin administration shifted the distribution of gaze toward a more balanced pattern of looking toward and away from the face of a live interaction partner, an effect not seen in the placebo group.
The four-week oxytocin administration period induced a relative increase in pupil dilation, interpreted as an index of heightened sympathetic arousal and attentional engagement.
The oxytocin-related increase in pupil dilation (autonomic responsivity) showed a moderate association with children's self-reported feelings of secure attachment.
SARS-CoV-2 S1 spike protein was found to persist within CD16+ monocytes for up to 15 months after infection in patients with Long COVID, despite no evidence of ongoing viral replication.
mRNA COVID-19 vaccination induced durable epigenetic reprogramming of monocyte-derived macrophages marked by increased H3K27 acetylation and elevated IL-1β and TNF-α production.

S1 and S2 spike protein fragments were detected in CD16+ monocytes 245 days after COVID-19 vaccination via mass spectrometry, in individuals with Long COVID-like symptoms lacking nucleocapsid antibodies.
Intermediate and non-classical monocytes express high levels of CCR5 and CX3CR1, promoting migration to and retention within previously inflamed tissues and vasculature.

Non-classical/intermediate monocytes harboring spike protein are associated with elevated IL-6, CCL5, and soluble CD40 ligand along with platelet and endothelial activation, features characteristic of PASC.

SARS-CoV-2 spike protein impairs lysosomal acidification and autophagosome-lysosome fusion in monocytes, reducing degradation of internalized viral antigens, an effect amplified in CD16+ non-classical monocytes.

In severe COVID-19, a delayed Type I interferon response precipitates infiltration of inflammatory monocyte-macrophages into the lungs, which secrete TNF, IL-6, and IL-1β, damaging vascular endothelium, causing alveolar leakage, and suppressing adaptive T-cell responses.

T-cell lymphopenia seen in severe COVID-19 may arise from hyperactivated myeloid-derived suppressor cells driving destructive inflammation within secondary lymphoid organs, collapsing normal T-cell development and survival.

In murine models, depletion of inflammatory monocyte-macrophages or ablation of Type I interferon signaling prevented death despite unchanged viral loads, indicating immune-mediated damage rather than viral replication drives severe disease pathology.
Persistent H3K27 acetylation after mRNA vaccination keeps immune genes such as IL1B, SYK, and NOD2 transcriptionally poised, producing a memory-like pro-inflammatory response upon restimulation.

Individuals with post-vaccination Long COVID-like symptoms exhibited the same inflammatory cytokine signature (IL-6, IL-8, CCL5, sCD40L) as infection-associated Long COVID and were misclassified as Long COVID patients by immune-based machine learning algorithms.

PET imaging studies in patients with acute and post-acute COVID showed increased labelled glucose uptake in the thoracic aorta, indicating elevated metabolic/inflammatory activity even without overt cardiovascular disease.
The CARTESIAN study observed rapid increases in pulse wave velocity post-COVID, equivalent to an increase of 5-7 years of vascular age within months.

SARS-CoV-2-related gut disruption is associated with microbiome dysbiosis characterized by overgrowth of Gram-negative bacteria such as Clostridia and depletion of commensals like Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus.

Renner et al. found hyper-reactivity of effector memory and tissue-resident memory CD8+ T cells with significant IL-3 production in patients recovering from mild COVID-19, persisting over time and associated with prolonged Long COVID-like symptoms.
MAIT cells, enriched at mucosal sites and capable of rapid cytokine release, are reported to be elevated in both Long COVID and ME/CFS.
Viral spike protein interacts with neuropilin-1, a surface molecule required for regulatory T cell stability and suppressive function, contributing to Treg dysfunction in Long COVID.
